memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Get out of our way," they replied. "This fellow came here as a foreigner, and now he wants to play the judge! We'll treat you worse than them." They kept bringing pressure on Lot and moved forward to break down the door. - Gen 19:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The mob turns on Lot. The moment he stands, however weakly, against their wickedness, their rage flares: "This fellow came here as a foreigner, and now he wants to play the judge!" They resent any hint of a moral standard, any suggestion that their behaviour is wrong. Even Lot's compromised protest is too much for them to bear.

This reveals something about the human heart in rebellion against God. People given over to sin often react to any moral challenge not with reflection but with fury. The mere presence of someone who won't join them feels like an accusation. Light exposes darkness, and darkness hates to be exposed.

Notice their words - "he wants to play the judge." They accuse Lot of judging them simply for not participating in their evil. This is an ancient pattern that still runs today: those who reject God's ways often recast any moral witness as arrogance or intolerance, and turn their anger on the messenger.

Jesus warned His followers to expect this: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first" (John 15:18). Standing for what is right will not always win applause; sometimes it provokes rage. But we are not called to be liked; we are called to be faithful. When truth provokes hostility, don't be surprised, and don't retaliate - respond as Christ did, with courage and grace, entrusting yourself to the God who judges justly (1 Pet 2:23).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you faced hostility simply for not going along with wrong?
- How can you respond to such rage with both courage and grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when standing for truth provokes anger, give me courage not to retreat and grace not to retaliate. Help me entrust myself to You, the God who judges justly, as Jesus did before me.
Amen.
